Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

We are looking for a Product Compliance Manager to join Veo's newly established Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) team.

As Veo continues to grow, we navigate a broad range of regulatory requirements across our products and business, from certifications, product safety, and environmental regulation to market access and broader compliance obligations.

In this role, you will focus on product-related regulatory compliance and certifications, while also working across Veo's broader compliance agenda. You will work closely with colleagues across Hardware, Product Development, Production, Procurement and other parts of the business to understand applicable requirements and help translate them into practical processes and solutions.

You will join a small GRC team with a broad mandate and significant exposure across Veo. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys understanding regulation, technology, and business.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Coordinate Veo's product certification and market-access activities across relevant markets, working closely with Hardware, Production and other internal stakeholders.

• Monitor and assess new and changing regulatory requirements relevant to Veo and help determine their practical implications for our products and business.

• Develop and maintain a structured overview of regulatory and certification requirements applicable to Veo's products throughout their lifecycle.

• Drive and coordinate implementation of regulatory and compliance requirements across relevant business functions, ensuring clear ownership, appropriate documentation and timely follow-up.

• Work with regulatory frameworks relevant to Veo's products, including areas such as product safety, batteries, electrical and electronic equipment, environmental requirements, waste and recycling obligations and related product compliance requirements.

• Coordinate with external certification bodies, laboratories, consultants and other specialists where required.

• Maintain and develop compliance documentation, certification records, technical files, declarations and other evidence required to demonstrate compliance.

• Support the assessment of regulatory and compliance implications when Veo enters new markets, introduces new products or makes material changes to existing products.

• Support Veo's broader compliance activities, including policies, procedures, monitoring, due diligence, risk assessments and training.

• Support customer, auditor and other stakeholder requests relating to compliance and certifications.

• Contribute to the continued development of Veo's broader GRC framework and take part in cross-functional compliance projects as required.

**Your qualifications:

**

• Relevant higher education in engineering, technology, law, business, quality/compliance, or another relevant discipline.

• Relevant professional experience within product compliance, regulatory compliance, certification, quality/regulatory affairs or a similar area, preferably from an international company.

• Experience working with regulatory requirements affecting hardware or electronic products is an advantage.

• Experience with one or more areas such as product safety, product certifications, battery regulation, electrical/electronic equipment regulation, environmental product requirements, waste/recycling regulation or similar regulatory regimes.

• Experience coordinating certification processes, testing, technical documentation, declarations or interactions with certification bodies and laboratories is highly relevant.

• Broader compliance experience, for example within sanctions and export controls, third-party due diligence, anti-bribery and corruption or other corporate compliance areas, is an advantage.

• An ability to understand complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical requirements for technical, operational and commercial teams.

• Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating initiatives across different functions and areas of expertise.

• A structured approach to documentation, monitoring and follow-up, combined with the ability to identify and prioritize material compliance risks.

• Strong business understanding and a pragmatic approach to compliance. You should be comfortable finding solutions that meet regulatory requirements while enabling the business to operate effectively.

• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership in an environment where processes and frameworks are still being developed.

• Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

At Veo, the Governance, Risk & Compliance team provides oversight, coordination and assurance across the company. We work closely with teams throughout Veo to ensure that regulatory requirements and risks are identified, appropriately owned and effectively managed.

You will report to the Head of Governance, Risk & Compliance and will have considerable opportunity to shape how Veo approaches compliance as the company continues to grow.

Contact Martin Eger Larsen one mel@veo.co if you have any questions

_Are you an experienced strategy consultant, ready to take full ownership of strategic projects and see your recommendations through to impact? Do you want to lead focused project teams and work closely with our senior leadership on key strategic projects? Are you ready to shape the strategic direction of a growing international green-tech company?

**Here Is What The Role Entails

**As our Strategy Manager, you will lead key strategic projects across Kamstrup, supported by a project team. You will own the projects end-to-end, from scoping and planning through analysis and recommendations to engaging the stakeholders who will implement them.

More specifically, you will be:

• Acting as project manager on selected strategic projects within or across business units, including scoping, planning, and day-to-day management of the project team

• Owning project deliverables, from analysis and problem-solving to communication of recommendations

• Facilitating workshops and strategic discussions with senior management and relevant subject matter experts

• Acting as a sparring partner and challenger to the business, ensuring that decisions rest on validated insights

• Contributing to the development of our internal ‘consultancy toolbox’, strategy frameworks and ways of working

This is an opportunity to work in time-boxed, agile projects, grounded in data-driven insights and close collaboration with the business. Unlike in consulting, you stay close to the organization after the final presentation and see the results of your work.

**Meet your future team

**With direct reference to Head of Strategy and Market Intelligence, you will become part of our Strategy and Market Intelligence team. We partner with Kamstrup’s senior leadership to shape the company’s strategic direction and deliver high-impact projects across the organization. The team is composed of passionate professionals with various backgrounds. Together we work professionally and with high ambition, while maintaining an informal and collaborative atmosphere, where sparring, openness and feedback are essential to how we grow and succeed together. We believe the strongest teams are built on diversity and inclusivity.

We see the team as a talent incubator, contributing to Kamstrup’s succession planning by developing future leaders who can drive sustainable growth.

**Less About Us, More About You

**We are looking for a Strategy Manager who has a structured and hypothesis-driven approach to problem-solving. You are proactive, and able to navigate complex challenges by turning data and insights into clear recommendations and tangible business outcomes.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Hold a relevant master's degree in e.g. business administration, economics, finance, or engineering with strong academic results

• Bring 3–5 years of experience in management consulting, or in a comparable role within an internal Strategy function including 1-2 years of experience leading strategic projects or workstreams with responsibility for team members and deliverables

• Possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills

• Excel in communication and interpersonal skills and the confidence to engage and challenge senior stakeholders

• Demonstrate a high level of proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint and AI tools

As we are an international organization it is important that you are fluent in English.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, you could still be a good candidate for the position. If you find the role intriguing, do not hesitate to apply.

**We are more than the ordinary workplace.

**We cherish the good colleagueship which we all contribute to, the only limit is your engagement. As we are a big organization youare bound to find one or more colleagues who share the same interest as you. This might be in our board game club, cycle team, during our yearly summer festival, or on the padel court. For example, our Head of System Engineering & IT DK is also our volunteer padel instructor while our Software Test Engineer runs weekly spinning classes.

Besides the best colleagues you could imagine, we also offer:

• Work life balance through flexible working hours

• Employee benefits include a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in-house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community

• Beneficial health care and insurance package

**Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

**Please submit your motivated resumé and transcript of records below. Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, and you can expect a response within six weeks.

The job is located at Kamstrup’s headquarters, in Stilling, Denmark.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Head of Strategy & Market Intelligence, Thomas Smith, on telephone number: +45 89 93 10 00

Based on your technical interests and expertise, you will join one of our operations teams, where you will take ownership of your own responsibilities while working closely with colleagues to deliver large-scale operational projects for our customers. About you

At Netcompany Operations, technical expertise and a passion for IT operations are at the core of what we do. As our new colleague, we hope you share that same enthusiasm.

Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**Genmab is looking for a Senior Operational Project Manager to join the Early-Stage CMC Project Management Department in Copenhagen.

Technical Operations is responsible for the development and manufacture of Genmab's antibody therapeutics supporting preclinical, clinical, and commercial programs. As part of Technical Operations, the Early-Stage CMC Project Management department drives CMC development programs from Discovery through Clinical Proof of Concept (Phase I/II), working closely with cross-functional experts and external partners.

As a Senior Operational CMC Project Manager, you will play a central role in translating CMC strategy into operational execution for development programs. You will be responsible for planning, coordinating, and driving day-to-day CMC activities while ensuring alignment across internal functions, external manufacturing partners, and project governance.

You will collaborate with specialists across Process Development, Analytical Development, Manufacturing, Product Characterization, Pharmaceutical Development, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Supply Chain, and other Technical Operations functions to successfully advance Genmab's pipeline.

You will become part of a highly collaborative team of experienced CMC Project Managers within Early-Stage CMC Project Management and report to the Team Lead, Early-Stage CMC Project Management.

**Responsibilities

**Your responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Drive the operational execution of integrated CMC development plans from Discovery through IND/CTA and early clinical development (Phase I/II).

• Develop, maintain, and execute integrated CMC project plans, including timelines, milestones, budgets, risks, deliverables, and resource planning.

• Coordinate day-to-day CMC activities across multiple technical disciplines and ensure effective collaboration between internal stakeholders and external partners.

• Manage operational interactions with Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs), Contract Development and Manufacturing Organizations (CDMOs), testing laboratories, and other external vendors.

• Monitor project progress, identify risks and issues proactively, facilitate mitigation plans, and ensure timely escalation when appropriate.

• Facilitate robust cross-functional communication and provide clear project status updates to project teams and governance forums.

• Coordinate preparation and review of CMC documentation supporting global regulatory submissions, including INDs, CTAs, and other health authority interactions.

• Coordinate and follow up on quality-related activities, including deviations, investigations, changes, CAPAs, and other quality events affecting project execution.

• Support project budget management, forecasting, governance activities, and overall project execution.

• Ensure project activities are conducted in compliance with Genmab's Quality Management System and applicable regulatory requirements.

• Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying opportunities to strengthen project management processes, tools, and ways of working within Early-Stage CMC Project Management.

**Requirements

**To succeed in this role, you bring a strong combination of scientific insight, project management expertise, and the ability to lead complex cross-functional collaborations.

**You Have

**

• A Master's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biotechnology, Chemical Engineering, or another relevant scientific discipline. A PhD or project management certification is considered an advantage.

• Approximately 8–10 years or more of relevant experience within CMC, biologics development, Technical Operations, or pharmaceutical development in the biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry.

• Demonstrated experience leading complex CMC development activities supporting biologics from early development through IND/CTA and Phase I/II clinical development.

• Strong project management experience, including planning, scheduling, budgeting, risk management, stakeholder management, and governance.

• Solid understanding of biologics process development, analytical development, GMP manufacturing, and CMC regulatory requirements.

• Experience working successfully with external manufacturing partners (CMOs/CDMOs) and outsourced development activities.

• Experience supporting regulatory CMC submissions and coordinating cross-functional deliverables.

• Strong communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills.

• Fluency in spoken and written English.

**The Following Experience Is Considered An Advantage

**

• Development and manufacturing of antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), or chemical engineering/API technology would be an asset

• Technology transfer between manufacturing sites or external partners.

• Experience working in an international matrix organization.

• Experience contributing to continuous improvement initiatives and implementation of project management tools or processes.

**We Are Looking For Someone Who

**

• Is an excellent collaborator and builds trusted relationships across functions and with external partners.

• Thrives in a dynamic environment while managing multiple priorities simultaneously.

• Takes ownership, demonstrates accountability, and proactively drives activities to completion.

• Has a structured, analytical, and solution-oriented approach to complex challenges.

• Communicates effectively with stakeholders at all organizational levels.

• Demonstrates sound judgment and maintains a strong quality mindset.

• Is curious, open-minded, and continuously seeks opportunities to improve processes and ways of working.

• Is motivated by delivering high-quality results that contribute to the success of Genmab and, ultimately, better outcomes for patients.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. With an IoT platform connecting more millions of devices, and growing - Trackunit is building the connectivity layer underneath the construction industry. Every one of those units carries a cellular radio, and every one of those radios sits inside a web of standards, type approvals, and patent licences that decides whether we can ship and where we can ship.

You will join our IoT Division, Device Reliability Engineering (DRE) team as an expert on IoT certifications, standards, and licensing including Standard Essential Patents (SEP). This position shapes both our exposure and our coverage arguments, and it means this role works in every direction at once, with suppliers, regulatory approvals, legal advisors, product and engineering, and with customers.

This is a role for someone who can hold a genuinely complex domain in their head and then explain it in three sentences to a customer who has never heard the phrase “patent exhaustion.”

Experience level: a deep specialist role. We expect solid, hands-on experience with cellular device approvals and licensing — likely 10+ years across regulatory, certification, or IP/licensing work in mobile, IoT, or telecom hardware. This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports, high autonomy, and direct executive visibility.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

****What's in it for you?

• A domain you will own, not administer. IoT Cellular License, SEP and certification strategy is an executive-level topic at Trackunit right now, with real financial exposure attached. You will not be filing paperwork in a corner, you will be shaping the position the company takes.

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

****What you'll do

****Your work splits roughly into four parts: licensing, approvals, guidance, and governance.

• Own our SEP position. Understand where our cellular SEP exposure actually sits across our device portfolio, track the relevant patent pools and licensing programmes, and maintain a clear, evidence-based view of what is covered through our supply chain and what is not.

• Run supplier licensing due diligence. Establish and maintain a consistent set of asks across module suppliers — coverage confirmation, standards and generations covered, and honest disclosure of known gaps — so responses can be compared side by side and fed into supplier qualification.

• Support licensing negotiations and claims. Work alongside our General Counsel, external patent counsel, and economic advisors on royalty basis questions, valuation and apportionment arguments, and claims that reach us through our OEM customers. You bring the technical and supply chain substance; they bring the legal strategy.

• Own global type approvals and certification. Plan and steer RED/CE, FCC, ISED, UKCA, and the wider set of regional approvals, plus GCF/PTCRB and carrier certification, across a multi-region device portfolio. Keep certification on the critical path of new product programmes rather than at the end of them.

• Stay ahead of regulatory change. Cyber Resilience Act, RED delegated acts, radio spectrum and network sunsets, environmental and product compliance requirements — know what is coming, when it bites, and what it means for our roadmap.

• Make the complex simple, and guide without over-promising. Write and maintain the internal playbooks, customer-facing explainers, and OEM guidance that turn this domain into something a commercial colleague or a customer can act on. Be the person Sales, Legal, and customers come to when a licensing notification lands, explaining the landscape accurately, saying clearly where the limits of our position are, and pointing customers to independent specialist advice where that is the right answer.

• Build the governance. Response protocols, decision records, escalation paths, and embedding licensing and compliance requirements into how we qualify suppliers and run the product development lifecycle.

****Who you are

****We think you'll need

• Strong working knowledge of cellular connectivity (e.g. LTE-M, NB-IoT, LTE Cat-1/1bis, 5G) and the direction of travel, plus a real understanding of the module and chipset landscape.

• Solid, practical experience with licensing and Standard Essential Patents in mobile or IoT devices: FRAND principles, patent pools, patent exhaustion and the limits of sublicensing, and how royalties are actually structured and argued.

• Hands-on experience with global type approvals and regulatory certification for radio products — RED/CE, FCC, and the regional approvals that come with selling hardware worldwide.

• Experience working across a hardware supply chain with module suppliers, test houses, notified bodies, and certification partners.

• Communication as a core skill, not a bonus. You can take a genuinely complicated subject and land it in plain language, in writing, with an audience that has no background in it.

• The judgement to know what we can and cannot say to a customer, and the discipline to hold that line even when it would be easier not to.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You are honest about uncertainty. In this domain, no one can offer a blanket guarantee, and the people who claim otherwise create problems later. We would rather be accurate than reassuring.

• You are curious and self-driven, this is a field that changes constantly, and nobody is going to hand you a reading list.

• You finish things. A clear one-page answer delivered this week beats a perfect analysis that arrives after the decision was made.

• You are comfortable being the only person in the room who knows a subject, and you use that position to make others smarter rather than to make yourself indispensable.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement, but a strong motivation and interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work, including MCP servers and agents against our own platform, and we see clear potential in applying it to research, documentation, and compliance workflows. We don't expect you to have experience with this but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

****How you'll grow here

****This is a specialist role with an unusually wide view of the business, and we've set it up that way on purpose.

• Executive proximity. You will work closely with the SVP of IoT Division, while reporting into a central function for IoT, as the Device Reliability Engineering. You will help in presenting to executive leadership on exposure, risk, and recommendations. Your analysis will inform on a product technical matter (Not Legal) but with real financial and commercial decisions.

• Cross-functional reach. Legal, Finance, Product Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Sales all depend on this domain. Few roles at Trackunit touch as many parts of the company.

• External network. You will work with external patent counsel, economic consultants, module suppliers, certification bodies, and industry forums — building a network that extends well beyond Trackunit.

• Room to define the function. This discipline is being built out now. What it becomes — and whether it grows into a team — is substantially yours to shape.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

Lead the team. Grow the business. Shape what comes next.

Are you ready to lead commercial growth across a diverse and important healthcare customer segment? This is a visible leadership role where strategy, customer insight and an engaged sales team come together with real ownership of commercial performance and the future direction of the business.

At Mediq Denmark, you will lead a team of 8 sales professionals supporting GP’s, specialist clinics and private hospitals. You will work closely with the Sales Director to turn market insight into action, strengthen customer partnerships and identify the opportunities that can move the segment forward.

This is a role for a leader who enjoys being close to the market. One day you may be shaping the sales strategy or challenging a business case; the next, joining a strategic customer discussion, coaching a colleague or turning a new idea into a practical growth plan.

Your impact

You will set the direction for the segment and translate ambition into profitable, sustainable growth. With ownership of the sales budget, forecast and commercial performance, you will keep customer value, market opportunities and team development firmly in focus.

• Develop and execute the sales strategy for GP’s, specialist clinics and private hospitals, supported by clear segmentation, targeting and account plans.

• Strengthen relationships across the customer landscape, from individual practices to strategic private hospital accounts, and take an active role in key negotiations and customer meetings.

• Use customer, market and competitor insight to identify growth opportunities, shape go-to-market plans and guide pricing and commercial decisions.

• Lead, coach and develop eight sales professionals, creating clear priorities, accountability and the confidence to perform at their best.

• Connect Sales with Category, Product Management and Sourcing to align the assortment, supplier strategy and commercial priorities around a strong customer experience.

What you bring

We are looking for a commercially curious and customer-focused sales leader who sees the bigger picture, acts with pace and brings people with them. You are comfortable moving between strategic business development and hands-on sales leadership, and you know when to explore the detail and when to step back and set direction.

• At least five years of documented experience in a comparable commercial and leadership role, including leading, coaching and developing sales professionals.

• A strong track record in sales execution, performance management and working with sales processes at both operational and strategic level.

• Strong commercial and analytical judgement, including the ability to develop and assess business cases and make sound pricing and growth decisions.

• Confident negotiation, presentation and stakeholder-management skills, supported by a structured and pragmatic approach to projects and processes.

• High energy, clear ownership and the ability to prioritise in a fast-paced and complex environment.

• Fluency in Danish and English. Experience from MedTech or the healthcare sector is an advantage.

Why join Mediq?

You will join a role where sales leadership is close to the action and your decisions will be visible. You will have the opportunity to influence commercial direction, build stronger customer partnerships and develop a team that can take this customer segment into its next chapter.

Our values - Customer Drive, Champion Spirit and Caring Heart - guide how we work, with a constant focus on creating value for patients.

Ready to lead the next stage of growth?

Bring your commercial leadership, customer focus and energy to Mediq. Help us strengthen the business, develop our people and build what comes next for customers across Denmark.

Location: Copenhagen Denmark.

Interested?

Submit your application through CareersatMediq.com or contact Artjoms.Bikovskis@Mediq.com, Talent Acquisition Partner Nordics and Baltics. We review every application with care and look forward to learning what you could bring to the future of Mediq Denmark.

We will be reviewing applications and interviewing candidates on a rolling basis as suitable candidates are identified. For this reason, we encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible.

About Mediq

Mediq is a leading European healthcare company with a 125-year legacy, operating in 14 countries with over 3,000 employees. Guided by our vision to enable sustainable healthcare, we focus on improving care outcomes and affordability through innovative products, services and solutions. Partnering with healthcare professionals across hospitals, clinics and home care, we help ensure patients receive the care they need to live independently, securely and feel more human.

At Mediq, we offer jobs that change lives. Join us.
